title: ETFs: a basket on the exchange
blurb: How an ETF differs from a mutual fund, what its price does during the day, and what trading costs.
t1.title: A basket you can trade
t1.hook: Asha has met mutual funds. Now she hears about ETFs. Your mission: find out what an ETF is, and how it differs from the fund she knows.
t1.define: An **ETF**, short for exchange-traded fund, is a basket of many things that trades on an exchange, like a share.
t1.analogy: Picture a ready-made thali you can swap with a friend at any time of day. A mutual fund's thali is handed out only once a day.
q1.opt.a: A basket of many things that trades on an exchange like a share
q1.opt.b: A loan you give to one company
q1.opt.c: A savings plan with a guaranteed return
q1.opt.d: One share of a single company
q1.fb.c: No ETF can guarantee a return. Its value moves with what is inside the basket.
q1.explain: An ETF is a basket that trades on an exchange, just like a share does.
q2.prompt: What is the main difference from a typical mutual fund?
q2.opt.a: An ETF is bought and priced during the day, like a share
q2.opt.b: An ETF holds only one company
q2.opt.c: An ETF is safer because it is on an exchange
q2.opt.d: An ETF is not a basket at all
q2.fb.c: Being on an exchange does not make it safer. What is inside the basket decides the risk.
q2.hint: Think about the thali swapped at any time of day.
q2.explain: The main difference is how it is bought and priced: during the day, like a share.
t2.title: Price during the day
t2.define: A mutual fund has one price a day, the day-end NAV. An ETF has a market price that moves while the exchange is open. Each ETF purchase also has a small **trading cost**.
t2.explore: Open the lab. Pick a time to buy the ETF and compare the units with the mutual fund.
q3.prompt: In the lab, buy the ETF at the 10am price. How many units does {amt} buy? Type a number.
q3.hint: Your money divided by the 10am price.
q4.prompt: How many units does the same {amt} buy in the mutual fund at its day-end price? Type a number.
q4.hint: Your money divided by the day-end price.
q5.prompt: What is the trading cost on the ETF purchase? Type a number in rupees.
q5.hint: Read the trading cost under the ETF in the lab.
q5.explain: The cost is {cost} of {amt}, which is {etfFee}.
t3.title: The same risk story
t3.define: An ETF is a wrapper. What is inside decides the risk. An ETF that follows an **index**, a list of companies, rises and falls with that list.
t3.note: Many index ETFs cost little each year. They still carry the ups and downs of what they hold.
q6.prompt: An ETF holds many companies. What does that mean for risk?
q6.opt.a: One failing company hurts less, but the ETF can still fall with the whole list
q6.opt.b: It has no risk at all
q6.opt.c: It has more risk than a single share
q6.fb.b: An ETF can fall whenever what it holds falls. Spreading lowers one risk, not all.
q6.fb.d: Nothing can only rise. Prices of what the ETF holds can fall, and so can the ETF.
q6.hint: Remember what spreading across many things can and cannot do.
q6.explain: Many companies in one basket soften one failure, but the whole list can still fall.
q7.prompt: What does an index ETF follow?
q7.hint: Reread the first card of this task.
q7.explain: An index ETF follows an index, which is a list of companies.
t4.title: Small regular amounts
t4.define: A SIP into a mutual fund is easy to set up. With an ETF, every purchase is its own trade, and each trade has a small cost.
t4.tradeoff: An ETF lets you pick the moment to buy. A mutual fund makes small regular buying simple. Which suits you depends on how you plan to invest.
q8.prompt: Asha buys {perBuy} of an ETF each month for {buys} months. Each buy costs {cost} of the amount. What is the total trading cost? Type a number in rupees.
q8.hint: The cost of one buy, times the number of buys.
q8.explain: Each buy costs {oneCost}. Over {buys} buys the cost is {planCost}.
q9.opt.a: Each ETF purchase is a trade, so many small buys add up in trading costs
q9.opt.b: ETFs have no costs at all
q9.opt.c: Mutual funds can be bought on the exchange all day
q9.opt.d: An ETF price never changes during the day
q9.hint: Think about what a trade costs.
q9.explain: Every ETF purchase is a trade with a small cost, so frequent small buys add up.
glossary.etf.def: A basket of many things that trades on an exchange like a share.
glossary.index.def: A list of companies used to measure or follow the market.
glossary.trading_cost.def: The small fee charged each time you buy or sell.
